# I'm So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now

**Oct 15, 2026 –Jan 11, 2027**

Explore an expanded history of Japanese photography through the work of twenty-eight intergenerational artists. Presented in partnership with Aperture.

[Learn More](https://www.icp.org/exhibitions/im-so-happy-you-are-here-japanese-women-photographers-1950s-now)

[Buy Tickets](https://buy.acmeticketing.com/orders/262/calendar)

# Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Failure

**Oct 15, 2026 –Jan 11, 2027**

Laia Abril examines how systems and institutions have failed victims of sexual violence for centuries through images, testimonies, archival materials, and multimedia installations.

[Learn More](https://www.icp.org/exhibitions/laia-abril-rape-and-institutional-failure)

[Buy Tickets](https://buy.acmeticketing.com/orders/262/calendar)

# ICP Spotlights 2026: Honoring Rinko Kawauchi

**December 9, 2026** 

Celebrate women in photography at ICP’s annual Spotlights Benefit. Join Rinko Kawauchi and Lesley A. Martin for a conversation over lunch while supporting ICP’s exhibitions and education programs.

[Learn More](https://www.icp.org/events/icp-spotlights-2026)

[Buy Tickets](https://givebutter.com/c/icps-2026-spotlights-benefit-copy-n68gxk)

## Photography Lives Here

The International Center of Photography is the world’s leading institution dedicated to photography and visual culture. Through exhibitions, education programs, community outreach, and public programs, ICP offers an open forum for dialogue about the power of the image, and is a gathering place for the photography community to meet, exchange ideas, and support one another.

Cameras and Coffee: Sony Sensor Cleaning and ICP's Open Education Showcase — Community Meet-Up (November 2026)

Thank you for your interest about Cameras and Coffee. This program is currently sold out. Walk-in is welcome within capacity and only Sony camera accepted for sensor cleansing without Cameras and Coffee registration. Connect with ICP's community during our monthly Cameras and Coffee social meet-up for photographers, collectors, and camera enthusiasts! This session of Cameras and Coffee, hosted by ICP’s open education and Lower East Side camera store, K&M, co presented with Sony. Stop by to connect and chat camera with photographer and ICP's faculty Roni Aviv and a Sony Artisan of Imagery Tony Gale.Stop by K&M store, 54 Orchard St, anytime from 10:30 AM to drop off your camera for a sensor cleaning, then meet us at ICP from 11 AM to 1 PM! Limit one camera per person, any brand welcome with Cameras and Coffee registration. Cameras and Coffee is held on the second Saturday of each month and free to attend with RSVP.The free ticket for Cameras and Coffee does not include access to the ICP Galleries. Added your museum admission ticket and stay later to view I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now and Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Failure. About the ArtistRoni Aviv is a photographer and educator living in Brooklyn, New York. Aviv works with photography, text, and mark-making to give form to a psychological space of re-processing experiences. She holds an MFA in Visual Arts from Columbia University. Aviv is an Adjunct Assistant Professor at Brooklyn College and the College of Staten Island, and a teaching artist with the Josephine Herrick Project and the International Center of Photography.Recent solo exhibitions include CEPA Gallery, NY and Real Art Ways, CT. Recent group exhibitions include Voltz Clarke Gallery, NY, The Bronx Museum, NY, Center for Book Arts, NY, Longwood Art Gallery, NY, and The Jewish Museum, NY. Aviv is a grant recipient of Artis Contemporary (2025, 2021) and the Foundation for Contemporary Arts (2024). Residencies and fellowships include NARS Foundation (2021), Center for Book Arts NY (2022), AIM Bronx Museum (2023), Centrum (2024), ProjectArt (2024-25), Constance Saltonstall Foundation for the Arts (2025), Ellis-Beauregard Foundation (2026), NooArts (2026) and Worthless Photographer in Residence (2026) Tony Gale is an award winning portrait photographer shooting for a range of advertising, editorial and corporate clients. Tony was raised in Bellingham, Washington (90 miles north of Seattle) and spent most of his time as a child exploring the woods behind his parents house. At 19 after visiting Bruce Lee's grave in Seattle, and taking his first photo with a disposable camera, he bought his first camera. He promptly broke it and bought his first SLR. At 21 he moved to Seattle to pursue photography and in fall of 2000 moved to NYC, the center of the world.Tony has taught photographic lighting at FIT in NYC and Parsons the New School for Design, judged photo contests, and has traveled the country leading workshops for American Photographic Artists and giving talks and presentations on photography.Tony is a Sony Artisan of Imagery and was the APA national president for six years. Special thanks to K&M for the generous public programs support.For over 50 years, K&M Camera has proudly served New York City's photography community as a trusted, family-owned camera store. Located in the Lower East Side, we offer an extensive selection of photo, video, audio, and production equipment, along with the city's largest collection of vintage cameras. We're committed to making the Lower East Side a vibrant hub for photography, creativity, and visual storytelling. Image by Scott Rudd.

Film Screening—Spirit of the Photobooth

Spirit of the Photobooth, is a new documentary that explores the history of the photobooth and the resurgence of classic booths all around the world. The film debuted at ICP in September 2026 on the 100-year anniversary of the opening of the first Photobooth and we are thrilled to offer a bonus screening.This program is free with museum admission. Film run time: 96 mins Image: Movie still from Spirit of the Photobooth, written and direct by Sam Anthony About the Film"2026 is the hundredth birthday of the photobooth. A fixture on Main Street, in malls, in the back of bars and in railway stations for decades, this overlooked and unsung part of photographic history looked set to be erased by the advent of the smartphone and The Selfie. But, that’s not the whole story.After all, who would pay and wait four minutes for self-portraits, when they could have as many as they like for free on their phone? For a while it didn’t look good for photobooths. The traditional analog booths, with their distinctive ‘real’ photographs were replaced by digital versions.Thousands of the old analog booths were destroyed or stuck in barns and warehouses.But 100 years after their invention, the ones that survived are now highly prized collectors items, using technology that has hardly changed and which still retains its old magic.Long lines of Gen Z users snake around the block in the world’s hippest cities to use them. And ironically, it’s digital technology and social media—on the face of it the booth’s greatest challenges—that have helped save them. Influencers have supercharged the vintage appeal of photobooths, and digital natives desperate for experiential “realness” have rediscovered the charms of holding four black and white shots in their hand after squeezing into the booth, drawing the curtain, and giving their best self to the camera. And most of them heard about it from some of the world’s biggest online celebrities.So now a new breed of ingenious photographic entrepreneurs have sprung up to service an insatiable demand. They scour the globe for old booths, restoring them to their former glory and spreading the word on Instagram and TikTok, because there’s money to be made: Big money.Truth is, there always was. When immigrant and inventor Anatol Josepho first launched the booth on Broadway in New York City on September 21, 1926, huge crowds gathered immediately, and he sold the patent six months later for an offer he couldn’t refuse.One hundred years later and the long lines have formed again, and the analog photobooth has never been hotter.So this is a film about how and why that happened. The story of the singular man who changed the way we take portraits, and the photobooth’s unique role in everything from the art of 1920s surrealists and Andy Warhol decades later, to the democratization of portraiture which gave the marginalized and overlooked a platform for photography on their own terms.Filmed all over the world, Spirit of the Photobooth is a social and cultural history as seen through the lens of the photobooth itself, and an account of photographic obsession that takes us to meet devotees in Australia, Europe, South Korea, and of course the United States.And it all starts with Anatol Josepho and his invention. A classic and extraordinary rags-to-riches origin story." —Sam Anthony, Writer and Director of Spirit of the Photobooth Image: Movie still from Spirit of the Photobooth, written and direct by Sam Anthony

84 Ludlow Street, New York, NY 10002

The Naomi Rosenblum ICP Talks Photographer Lecture Series with Ishiuchi Miyako and Katayama Mari

Join us for the next fall Naomi Rosenblum ICP Talks lecture of the year featuring world renowned photographers Ishiuchi Miyako and Katayama Mari, moderated by curator Pauline Vermare. Both artists will discuss the wide-ranging scope of their career, including both Katayama’s and Ishiuchi's work on view in our current exhibition I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now.This program is being offered both in person at ICP, located on NYC's Lower East Side, and online. Current ICP students and faculty of the One-Year Certificate programs are automatically enrolled and invited to attend all lectures.Past speakers of the Naomi Rosenblum ICP Talks Lecture series include: JEB, Philip Cheung, Donna Ferrato, Naima Green, David Alekhuogie, Keisha Scarville, Roe Ethridge, and Erin Schaff. About the Series:The 2026-2027 Naomi Rosenblum ICP Talks Photographer Lecture Series is made possible through generous support from the Rosenblum Family. Additional support for this program was provided by the Japan Foundation, New York and for Ishiuchi Miyako, by Marukawa Collection.ICP is thrilled to honor Naomi Rosenblum’s contribution to the field and to further her life’s work through this lecture series. Naomi Rosenblum was one of the leading photography historians of her generation and the author of A World History of Photography and A History of Women Photographers. The 2025-2026 Naomi Rosenblum ICP Talks Photographer Lecture Series is made possible through generous support from the Rosenblum Family. About the Speakers:Ishiuchi Miyako (born in Kiryū, Japan, 1947) is a Japanese photographer based in Gunma prefecture. She has been the recipient of numerous awards, including the Kimura Ihei Memorial Photographic Award (1978) and the Hasselblad Award (2014). Her work is included in collections worldwide.Katayama Mari is a multidisciplinary artist based in Gunma, Japan. Born in 1987 in Saitama, she graduated with a Master’s degree from the Department of Intermedia Art at Tokyo University of the Arts in 2012. Katayama’s artistic practice begins with intricately hand-sewn fabric objects which feature in her photography, video, and activist art projects. She uses her body as a living sculpture, a mannequin and a lens through which to reflect society and our environment.Pauline Vermare is the Phillip and Edith Leonian Curator, Photography, Brooklyn Museum. Previously, she served as the cultural director of Magnum Photos in New York, and curator at the International Center of Photography and the Museum of Modern Art, New York.Header Image: Ishiuchi Miyako, Mother’s #39, 2002. Courtesy Third Gallery Aya, Osaka, and Aperture About the ExhibitionI’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now reconsiders and expands on the history of Japanese photography through the work twenty-eight intergenerational artists from the 1950s to today. Presented in partnership with Aperture and curated by Pauline Vermare, Lesley A. Martin, and Takeuchi Mariko, the exhibition includes work by Fujioka Aya, Hara Mikiko, Hiromix, Ishikawa Mao, Ishiuchi Miyako, Katayama Mari, Kawauchi Rinko, Komatsu Hiroko, Kon Michiko, Nagashima Yurie, Narahashi Asako, Ninagawa Mika, Nishimura Tamiko, Noguchi Rika, Nomura Sakiko, Okabe Momo, Okanoue Toshiko, Onodera Yuki, Sawada Tomoko, Shiga Lieko, Sugiura Kunié, Suzuki Nozomi, Tawada Yuki, Tokiwa Toyoko, Ushioda Tokuko, Watanabe Hitomi, Yamazawa Eiko and Yanagi Miwa.Spanning photography, installation, photobooks, and printed matter, the exhibition explores the experiences and perspectives of women in Japan through delicate and blunt observations of everyday life, critical reflections on the roles inhabited and reshaped by Japanese women, and approaches that push the boundaries of photography. The exhibition is accompanied by a major publication (Aperture, 2024) that expands upon content of the show through essays, historical material, and a comprehensive bibliography of photobooks made by Japanese women.

Welcome to Woodmere, where we tell the stories of the [art](https://woodmeremuseum.org/art) and [artists](https://woodmeremuseum.org/collection) of Philadelphia. We invite you to explore our [exhibitions](https://woodmeremuseum.org/exhibitions), and experience [art](https://woodmeremuseum.org/art), [music](https://woodmeremuseum.org/happenings/jazz-at-woodmere), [film](https://woodmeremuseum.org/happenings/film), [nature](https://woodmeremuseum.org/woodmeres-outdoor-wonder), and horticulture across our ten acres of [grounds](https://woodmeremuseum.org/woodmeres-outdoor-wonder). Tap into your own creative energy through our [classes](https://woodmeremuseum.org/learn-create), [resources](https://woodmeremuseum.org/learn-create/teaching-resources), and [public programs](https://woodmeremuseum.org/calendar). Explore distinct experiences at Charles Knox Smith Hall and [Frances M. Maguire Hall](https://woodmeremuseum.org/maguire-hall-project).

[BECOME A MEMBER!](https://woodmeremuseum.org/become-a-member)

[One Museum, two experiences](https://woodmeremuseum.org/about/two-experiences) [Interactive map](https://woodmeremuseum.org/interactive-map)

### Arc of Promise

In celebration of America’s 250th anniversary, Arc of Promise explores how Philadelphia’s artists have envisioned “America” as an idea, from the nation’s founding to today.

[Learn more](https://woodmeremuseum.org/exhibitions/arc-of-promise)

## Collection spotlights

[View all collection spotlights](https://woodmeremuseum.org/collection)

Consisting of over 11,000 objects, Woodmere holds one of the world's great collections of American art, centered on the art and artists of Philadelphia throughout our city's history. 
Check out our collection spotlights below, or [view the collection](https://woodmeremuseum.org/collection).

Woodmere’s Outdoor Wonder, Grounds

### Sculpture and Nature

Woodmere's Outdoor Wonder presents significant examples of public sculpture set in harmony with our grounds and gardens. The museum's founder, Charles Knox Smith, found deep spiritual meaning in the beauty and cycles of nature. Today, Woodmere recognizes the Lenape people as the original inhabitants of Pennsylvania, and with their partnership seeks to be a steward of the land, water, and sky of Lenapehoking, their ancestral homeland.

[Explore](https://woodmeremuseum.org/collection-spotlights/sculpture-and-nature)

Charles Knox Smith Hall

### Founder's Collection

Woodmere's founder, Charles Knox Smith (1845–1916), assembled a collection that attests both the tumultuous history of his era and his abiding belief in art as a vehicle for spiritual and patriotic uplift.

[Explore](https://woodmeremuseum.org/collection-spotlights/founders-gallery)

Frances M. Maguire Hall

### Arthur Carles and His Circle

Arthur B. Carles immersed himself in the Parisian avant-garde, absorbing the ideas animating movements like fauvism and cubism. He carried this vital new artistic language back to Philadelphia, where he inspired his students to forge their own modernist paths.

[Explore](https://woodmeremuseum.org/collection-spotlights/arthur-carles)

SHOP!

Step into our glittering gallery & shop festive gifts for kids, family, friends, and yourself! This annual pop-up store takes place at Smith Hall and does not require admission to shop. Open November 19 through January 3 during museum hours!

[Learn more](https://woodmeremuseum.org/store)

10:30 AM – 12:00 PM10:30 – 12:0010:30 AM – 12:00 PM

Adaptive Art takes place on the second Friday of each month, from 10:30 am – 12 pm.

Adaptive Art is a monthly visual arts and creativity class designed for adults (18+) with disabilities. Thanks to a generous grant from Ronald McDonald House Charities, registration is currently free while funds last. In this class, participants will explore various adaptive mediums such as movement, drawing, painting, and poetry to find new ways of self-expression and PLAY alongside talented and passionate teacher, Sara Fisher. Don't miss this opportunity to discover the joy of art in a supportive and inclusive environment.

**Parking & Accessibility Notice** 

Please note Adaptive Art program on August 14th takes place during CelebrateErie, when downtown Erie experiences increased traffic, road closures, and larger crowds. _As a result, navigating to the Museum may take a little longer than usual and may present additional accessibility considerations for some participants._ 

We recommend allowing extra travel time and parking in the 5th & Peach Parking Garage, which offers convenient access to the Museum. 
We appreciate your patience and look forward to welcoming you!

# Abbeys, Barns, and Churches: Drawings of Medieval Architecture by Ernest Born

[VIEW DETAILS](https://www.timkenmuseum.org/#)

Artist-in-residence: july 8-10, 2026 
vip member preview reception: july 12, 2026 
On View July 15–September 6, 2026

October

7

to

February 28, 2027

This fall, the Timken Museum of Art invites visitors to view the Middle Ages through adistinctly modern eye. Abbeys, Barns, and Churches, The Building Blocks of Medieval Architecture, an exhibition of drawings by California architect Ernest A. Born, opens October 7, 2026 and remains on view through January 31, 2027 in the Timken's intimate galleries in Balboa Park. Comprising more than 20 meticulous studies in ink, chalk, pastel, and pencil, the exhibition follows one of California's singular architectural minds as he traces the appearance of stone barns, sprawling abbeys, and small parish churches of Europe.

[Learn more](https://www.timkenmuseum.org/news/abbeys-barns-and-churches-drawings-of-medieval-architecture-by-ernest-born)

## About El Museo

Founded in 1969, El Museo del Barrio’s mission is to present and preserve the art and culture of Puerto Ricans and all Latin Americans in the United States. 

[Learn More >](https://elmuseo.org/history-mission/)

New York, NY 10029

# WELCOME TO MOCA JACKSONVILLE

Explore the art, artists, and ideas of our time in the heart of Downtown Jacksonville! Kaloust Guedel: Where Time Bends Softly

[Kaloust Guedel: Where Time Bends Softly](https://oma-online.org/kaloust-guedel/)

[Explore the intersection of ancient techniques and contemporary art in an immersive exhibition where fiber, material, and craftsmanship blur the boundaries between past and present.](https://oma-online.org/kaloust-guedel/)

[Learn More](https://oma-online.org/kaloust-guedel/)

Rupinder Kaloti: The Gathering

[Rupinder Kaloti: The Gathering](https://oma-online.org/rupinder-kaloti/)

[Experience this vibrant, large-scale exploration of the Punjabi-American immigrant experience. Moving beyond familiar narratives of immigrant struggle, the work imagines a vivid world that appears after hardship has passed.](https://oma-online.org/rupinder-kaloti/)

[Learn More](https://oma-online.org/rupinder-kaloti/)

Soft Power: On Color, Time, and Resistance

[Soft Power: On Color, Time, and Resistance](https://oma-online.org/2026-art-prize/)

[We're pleased to present the 2026 annual exhibition of the San Diego Art Prize featuring the work of this year’s esteemed recipients, Danielle Dean, Ingrid Hernández, and Tatiana Ortiz-Rubio, in collaboration with San Diego Visual Arts Network.](https://oma-online.org/2026-art-prize/)

[Learn More](https://oma-online.org/2026-art-prize/)

Changing Terrain: Regional Artists Interpret Our Landscape

[Changing Terrain: Regional Artists Interpret Our Landscape](https://oma-online.org/changing-terrain/)

headings.text: BRINGING PEOPLE TOGETHER TO EXPLORE THE ART AND STORIES OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ARTISTS.
Kaloust Guedel: Where Time Bends Softly
Soft Power: On Color, Time, and Resistance
Changing Terrain: Regional Artists Interpret Our Landscape

Relax over a steaming cup of coffee, and bring your artwork to share with your fellow Artist Alliance members! Each month one artist will have the opportunity to give a longer presentation, and practice sharing their work and ideas in front of a supportive group setting.
This month's presenter has yet to be determined!
*To be selected as a future presenter, please submit your name and website to cathy@artstudiosandiego.com.

In this virtual workshop series, artists are invited to turn their journal into a studio companion and idea incubator. Through interactive Zoom sessions we'll explore simple, repeatable practices artists can use to generate content, clarify ideas, and deepen connection to their work.
NOVEMBER TOPIC: HOW TO UNDERSTAND YOUR STORY
In this interactive journaling workshop, you’ll:
- Explore your core values and creative motivations
-Use guided journaling prompts to uncover your personal “Why”
-Shape words that inspire your art, fuel your career, and connect you with audiences
You will receive a Zoom link in the emailed RSVP confirmation receipt.

Artist Alliance members, along with their guests, are welcome to engage in a group art share and critique, aimed at fostering professional growth. Not yet part of the alliance? No worries, you can join either before the event or on-site!
Kick off your weekend with a bite-sized happy hour version of our renowned Studio Arts workshops. Gather with friends in an artistic space designed to amplify your creative side.

Join arts educator Robin Douglas, as we dip our toes into the work of celebrated artists over drinks and nibbles, followed by a rapid demonstration of their styles. You’ll then be guided to interpret these artists and create your own singular, spectacular work of art. We’ll help you express your unique style and ensure you have a blast doing it.

Using rich papers and photo images, text, and color media, you will create an original thought-provoking masterpiece at this workshop. Different presentation techniques will be explored. A fantastic skill-building opportunity!
All levels of experience are encouraged to participate. OMA provides food, drinks and supplies; all you have to do is get yourself out of work, grab your friends, and have fun!

Come paint the Oceanside Pier at the end of Pier View Way or the surrounding Oceanside beach shops and coastline! We'll meet at the start of the Pier at 2:00pm and fan out from there. Free parking is available at the lot at the corner of Seagaze and S Cleveland Drives or metered parking can be found immediately adjacent to the Pier. Public restrooms are available.

Whether you're a seasoned plein air painter or just starting your artistic journey, this event is for you! Beginners and experienced painters can find fresh inspiration in the urban and natural landscape.
Register for the event on the San Diego Plein Air Painters Meetup Group site: https://www.meetup.com/painter-86/
Bring your painting supplies, easel, and canvases. Don't forget sunscreen and a hat for the California sun!
Paint to your heart's content and enjoy the dynamic surroundings.
Become an OMA Artist Alliance Member:
Join and learn more about Artist Alliance and the activities at Oceanside Museum of Art at: https://oma-online.org/membership/

OMA members, this one's for you! Celebrate Small Business Saturday with a little holiday shopping at The Museum Store. Enjoy an extra 10% off all day (up to 20% total savings!) and shop a curated selection of gifts made by local artists.

Be there for the first hour, from 10:00–11:00am, for mimosas, a few special surprises, and a FREE limited-edition mini OMA tote for the first 20 shoppers through the door! Mark your calendar and start planning your shopping with the 2026 Holiday Gift Guide.

Have someone a bit harder to shop for? Purchase a gift membership for someone special (or upgrade your own OMA membership!) to receive exclusive, member-only merch, now through December 31, 2026! Place your order at our Member Holiday Shopping event, inquire at the front desk, or email Anna Antenucci at anna@oma-online.org to upgrade. Member keychains and embroidered OMA sweatshirts are available at select levels:

OMA Keychain: Available with gift membership or personal upgrades to Basic for One, Basic for Two, or Patron Level. (Available for pickup at the time of purchase at the OMA front desk or The Museum Store.)

Embroidered OMA Sweatshirt: Available with gift memberships or personal upgrades to President's Circle through Director's Circle. (Requires size and color at time of purchase. Sweatshirt will be shipped to OMA for pickup.)

OMA Artist Alliance members and their guests are invited to gather each month for a lively social meetup hosted in San Diego and North County. These informal get-togethers offer a relaxed opportunity to connect with fellow artists, share ideas, and build community while exploring a range of hotspots across the region. Whether you’re catching up with familiar faces or meeting someone new, each gathering encourages conversation, collaboration, and camaraderie within the Artist Alliance network.
This is a no-host event, attendees are welcome to purchase their own food and beverages.
Get art delivered to your inbox.
Make your inbox the intersection of Southern California art and everyday. Receive updates on our exhibitions, programs, and special events.

 ### [The Spirit of Invention: Patent Office and Patentees](https://npg.si.edu/exhibition/spirit-invention-patent-office)

 Timed with the U.S. semiquincentennial, the National Portrait Gallery commemorates the founding of its historic home with “The Spirit of Invention: Patent Office and Patentees.”  This exhibition sketches the early history of the Patent Office—the third oldest building in Washington—through works in the museum’s collection.

- [black and white photo of a woman in a dress holding flowers](https://npg.si.edu/exhibition/meserve-collection-highlights-modern-prints-mathew-brady%E2%80%99s-portrait-negatives)

 The Portrait Gallery’s vast collection of Civil War-era, portrait negatives is represented in this exhibition through nine modern prints from Mathew Brady’s (c. 1823–1896) original photographic negatives. Portraits of Abraham Lincoln, Nathaniel Hawthorne, Ulysses Grant, and Emma, Queen of Hawai’i are featured, along with an original, glass-plate negative and one of Brady’s wooden storage boxes.

## #myNPG

[smithsoniannpg](https://www.instagram.com/smithsoniannpg/)

When the National Portrait Gallery was founded by an act of Congress in 1962, photographs were excluded from its collection. After the Portrait Gallery opened its doors to the public in 1968, the inability to acquire photographic portraits emerged as a serious shortcoming. Without the inclusion of photographs, countless individuals who shaped the nation’s history could not be represented simply because a painted or sculpted likeness did not exist. 

In 1976, the Portrait Gallery amended its charter and began collecting photographs. 

Now open: “Photographic Memory: Fifty Years of Collecting,” featuring portraiture from the dawn of photography to the present day. This exhibition marks the fiftieth anniversary of the founding of the National Portrait Gallery’s photography collection.

## [Sebastian Thomas: Always the Moon and the Sun](https://arts.pepperdine.edu/museum/2026-2027/sebastian-thomas.htm)

**August 25, 2026–March 27, 2027**

Sebastian Thomas is an American painter whose work reimagines medieval iconography through a contemporary lens, blending mythic storytelling with reflections on modern culture. Drawing from illuminated manuscripts, altar paintings, and devotional objects, he creates densely composed works made of multiple panels that stage vivid encounters between saints, beasts, and heroes, using allegories to communicate ideas that resonate across centuries. His intricate surfaces and luminous palettes merge the richness of International Gothic painting with the wit and irreverence of popular culture.

Thomas formulates his own casein paints using traditional methods, treating craftsmanship as an act of devotion. Many of his works are assembled from interlocking panels connected with French cleats, a modular format that allows for reconfiguration and narrative play. Across these ornate tableaux, female protagonists including martyrs, sphinxes, and warriors emerge as central figures, embodying intelligence, resilience, and spiritual agency. By reviving premodern visual languages, Thomas critiques the technological and social hierarchies of the present, envisioning a world where mythic imagination resists digital domination.

This year’s Annual Fund is more critical than ever. As we step into this breathtaking new era, your support ensures that our exhibitions soar, our educational programs thrive, and our new space lives up to its full potential.

### **will you help us get to the next level?**

[Learn More](https://www.hickoryart.org/20262027annualfund)

The right outfit can open doors, build confidence, and help someone take the next step toward a brighter future. But, professional clothing can be a barrier for those entering the workforce or pursuing new career opportunities. Hickory Museum of Art, in partnership with local organizations, is collecting professional clothing to help community members look and feel their best as they pursue their career goals.

## Help Someone Dress for Success

**_Clothing Donations Needed_**

We welcome new or gently used men’s and women’s business casual and professional attire in all sizes and for all seasons, including:

- Men’s & women’s suits

- Men’s & women’s button-down shirts

- Polo shirts

- Women’s dresses & skirts

- Men’s & women’s pants

- Men’s & women’s shoes

- Belts

**_Donation Guidelines_**

- Clothing should be no more than five years old and reflect current styles.

- All clothing must be clean and free of stains and tears.

- Please bring clothing on hangers.

**_Where to Donate_**

Drop off donations at the Hickory Museum of Art business office on the third floor, November 11–18, from 9 AM-4 PM.

Questions? Contact Jenny Cody at [jcody@hickoryart.org](mailto:jcody@hickoryart.org).

## Stories to Tell

The Art Museum has more than 4,000 paintings, prints, works on paper, sculpture, and ceramics with messages for you from across the globe and over the centuries.

[Take a look at our collection](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/the-collection)

## Past Exhibitions

[Read More: Material Matters](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/material-matters 'Read More: Material Matters')

### [Material Matters](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/material-matters 'Read More: Material Matters')

This exhibition, Material Matters, centers on the premise of the shared heritage of Africa and the African-diaspora; purpose and message come first.

[Read More: Material Matters](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/material-matters)

[Read More: Soft/Cover](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/soft-cover 'Read More: Soft/Cover')

### [Soft/Cover](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/soft-cover 'Read More: Soft/Cover')

Soft/Cover surveys the many surprising ways artists have used fabric and screen-printing to create objects that relate to the body, focusing on the relationship of textiles to fashion and architecture.

[Read More: Soft/Cover](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/soft-cover)

[Read More: Gamaliel Rodriguez: Topographies of Memory](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/gamaliel-rodriguez-topographies-of-memory 'Read More: Gamaliel Rodriguez: Topographies of Memory')

### [Gamaliel Rodriguez: Topographies of Memory](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/gamaliel-rodriguez-topographies-of-memory 'Read More: Gamaliel Rodriguez: Topographies of Memory')

Topographies of Memory is the first mid-career survey of works by artist Gamaliel Rodgriguez. Known for his striking use of color; monochromatic palette; and eerily familiar, yet non-descript landscapes, Rodgriguez’s practice pushes the boundaries of drawing.

[Read More: Gamaliel Rodriguez: Topographies of Memory](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions/gamaliel-rodriguez-topographies-of-memory)

[View all past exhibitions](https://artmuseum.wvu.edu/art/past-exhibitions)

## About the Artists

Each semester we explore the inspiration behind the exhibitions.

### Gamaliel Rodgriguez

Topographies of Memory is the first mid-career survey of works by artist Gamaliel Rodgriguez. Known for his striking use of color; monochromatic palette; and eerily familiar, yet non-descript landscapes, Rodgriguez’s practice pushes the boundaries of drawing. Rodriguez has spent much of his career examining the complexities of history, both the clarity and vagueness of memory, the fragile state of infrastructures within society, and the balance between humankind and nature. His works place these elements in conversation with one another, using his distinct aesthetic to highlight their evolving power dynamic.

[Watch other Artist Statements](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLwVC6cExv_cdiQg32OXrA0opOegX6-r_5)

# IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts (MoCNA)

The IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts (MoCNA) is the country’s leading museum for exhibiting, collecting, and interpreting the most progressive work of contemporary Indigenous artists. The museum is dedicated solely to advancing the scholarship, discourse, and interpretation of contemporary Native art for all audiences. The museum stewards over 9,500 artworks in all media created from 1962 to the present day. MoCNA is at the forefront of contemporary Native art presentations and strives to be flexible, foresighted, and risk-taking in its exhibitions and programs. MoCNA is in the heart of downtown Santa Fe, New Mexico, 108 Cathedral Place, 87501.

- [Mission](https://iaia.edu/mocna/#)
- [History](https://iaia.edu/mocna/#)

### Mission

MoCNA’s Mission: To elevate contemporary Indigenous art through exhibitions, collections, programs, partnerships, and new research.

### History

The IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts (MoCNA) collection originated from the Institute of American Indian Arts’ student honors program, along with donations by artists and private collectors, and became the catalyst for the museum’s establishment in 1972. Until IAIA acquired the federal building in downtown Santa Fe in 1990, exhibitions were limited to borrowed spaces on the Santa Fe Indian School campus, and the collection remained in storage. Following years of neglect and stylistic deterioration, the building was transformed into a major Native art museum. Architects preserved the exterior of the 1922 Pueblo Revival–style building and completely renovated the interior. The space underwent a major renovation in 2004 and reopened in mid-2005 as a vibrant venue for exhibitions, educational programming, and cross-cultural dialogue. In 2010, the permanent collection moved from the museum to a new facility on IAIA’s campus, the Science and Technology Building, located 12 miles south of downtown. The new state-of-the-art facility occupies 7,000 square feet and promotes best practices in collection care. The relocation of the collection provided space for the museum to open a collection-based gallery named the Kieve Family Gallery.

### Visit

Schedule a visit to the IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts (MoCNA) to experience the latest exhibitions of contemporary Native art. Voted #3 Best Art Museum in the country by USA Today 10Best Readers’ Choice in 2021 and 2023, the museum presents Indigenous art globally. For questions, please contact the museum store at [store@iaia.edu](mailto:store@iaia.edu) or call (505) 428-5912.

- $10: General
- $5: Student (valid ID)
- $5: Senior (62 or older)
- $5: Disabled People (Caregivers accompanying disabled visitors receive complimentary admission.)
- $5: New Mexico Resident
- Free: Children (under 16), MoCNA Members, Native and Indigenous Peoples, and United States Military Veterans
- Free Fridays for all guests

##### Accessibility

MoCNA presents films with closed and SDH (subtitles for the deaf and hard-of-hearing) captioning whenever possible. If you have questions, please call (505) 428-5912 or email [store@iaia.edu](mailto:store@iaia.edu).

Here is a listing of existing accommodations that the museum is currently providing.

- Automated main entrance doors
- Accessible ramps (exterior corner of San Francisco and Cathedral)
- Wheelchair (available if needed)
- Accessible restrooms
- Accessible elevator
- Galleries, store, and hallways are accessible
- Access for service animals

The museum is committed to addressing accessibility concerns in a timely manner. Please use the form on the IAIA’s [Accessibility](https://iaia.edu/accessibility/) page to report barriers that you have encountered in our services, programs, activities, or facilities at the museum.
